Help & Support

Add your first pet, get to know the everyday care tools, and learn how to move your data to a new iPhone.

Getting startedFAQTroubleshooting

Getting started

Add a pet
Open Pets and tap Add in the bottom-right corner. Enter a name and species. You can add a photo, birthday, and health information later.
Log care and health
Open Care to log daily activities or find records for vaccinations, deworming, medication, vet visits, and weight. Open Today to see your schedule and mark tasks complete.
Manage stock and spending
Open Supplies to switch between your inventory, shopping list, and expenses. Add a purchase to your inventory and record the expense from the shopping list.
Back up before switching phones
On your old iPhone, open Settings → Data & Backup → Export Full Backup. Save the ZIP somewhere you can access from your new device. On your new iPhone, choose Import from Backup, select the ZIP, review the preview, and confirm.

Frequently asked questions

What’s included in the free app and PawTale+?

With the free app you can add or reactivate one active pet, track daily care, health and expenses, read all of PawWiki, export a vet summary image, and use full ZIP backups. PawTale+ unlocks more pets, iCloud sync, calendar integration, vet PDFs, handover exports, full canvas creation, and more widgets and appearance options. Check the App Store for prices and trial eligibility.

Do I need an account? How do I sync my devices?

You don’t need a PawTale account. iCloud Sync requires an active PawTale+ subscription. Use the same Apple Account and enable Settings → Data & Backup → iCloud Sync on both devices. With Auto Sync off, tap Sync Now when needed. ZIP backup and import are available to all users.

How do I restore purchases or manage auto-renewal?

Tap Restore Purchases on the PawTale+ screen using the App Store account that made the purchase. Tap Manage Subscription there or open iOS Settings → Apple Account → Subscriptions to turn off auto-renewal. You keep access until the end of the current subscription period. Apple Standard Terms of Use

What happens to my pets, canvas projects, and iCloud data when my subscription ends?

You can still view, care for, and back up existing pets. Adding or reactivating pets is subject to the free limit. You can view and re-export finished canvas projects. Drafts remain saved and require an active subscription to edit. iCloud Sync and calendar updates pause while local data, cloud copies, and existing calendar events remain. See the privacy policy for cloud copies.

What’s in a backup? Will importing overwrite my records?

A full ZIP covers pet profiles, care records, reminders, expenses, albums, and related photos. It can also include canvas projects and stickers. A standalone v2 JSON restores the care data in that file. Import skips identical items by ID and reports conflicts if the same ID has different content. The free app can restore existing pet profiles from a multi-pet backup.

Why doesn’t PawTale ask to access my entire photo library?

iOS lets PawTale read the photos you select. Saving a canvas export to Apple Photos may require permission to add photos.

Troubleshooting

My devices aren’t updating

Check that PawTale+ is active. On both devices, check that you’re using the same iCloud account and have enabled iCloud Sync, then check the network connection and available iCloud storage. Close any open editor, then tap Sync Now. If the issue persists, run Advanced Diagnostics and share only the relevant message with support.

I’m not getting reminders

Check that notifications are enabled for the task and that the scheduled time is correct. Then check Settings → Privacy & Security → System Permissions in PawTale. If access is allowed, check Focus, Scheduled Summary, and the app’s notification settings in iOS.

My backup won’t import

Use a ZIP from Export Full Backup or a complete v2 JSON file. Older v1 JSON, CSV, and individual pet reports cannot be restored. If the file is in cloud storage, check that it has finished downloading in Files. If the preview reports a conflict, keep the original backup and existing records, and send the error message to support.

I can’t save a canvas image to Photos

Choose Save to Photos from the canvas share menu. Check in iOS Settings whether PawTale can add photos. You can also save the project to Files from the share menu.
